faq.a: The number of months your cash lasts before it falls to the reserve you want to keep, if costs and revenue stay the same. Cash on hand minus the reserve, divided by the monthly net burn (costs minus revenue), gives the months of runway.
Then your net burn is zero or negative, and the runway is indefinite at current rates. This tool says so plainly instead of showing a made-up number of months.
faq.q: What if my revenue covers my costs?

faq.a: The cash you want to keep untouched, for example one month of payroll or an emergency cushion. The runway ends when cash reaches that level, not when it reaches zero.
No, it is a steady-rate estimate. Real costs and revenue change every month, so re-run it whenever either moves.

title: Cash Runway Calculator | ToolVerse
whenNotToUse: This tool assumes the same monthly costs and revenue every month. Real businesses are lumpy, so the date is an estimate.
It does not include taxes, loan payments, or one-off costs unless you include them in the monthly burn.
It is a planning estimate, not a cash flow forecast or financial advice.
